sampling_model.design: A blinded two-arm randomized trial with a separate blinded gold-standard validation sample.
sampling_model.units: Trial and validation samples have fixed positive sizes \(n_0,n_1,m_1,m_0\); the four stated marginal count laws are sufficient, with no mutual-independence requirement among the counts.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary randomized assignment \(A\) with positive allocation probability in each arm.
sampling_model.overlap: The assay satisfies the uniform informativeness restriction \(s+c-1\ge\kappa>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Two-sided Clopper--Pearson intervals are formed separately for \(q_0,q_1,s,c\) and intersected with the fixed assay rectangle before projection.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A binary joint table can be recovered from its two margins and a fixed positive odds ratio.
Direct misclassification writes the observed and latent discrete distributions as a linear system with a restricted channel matrix.

For symbolic ordinal benefit bounds, the regular bootstrap can undercover near parameter-space boundaries, while an \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap correction is conservative in the reported simulations.
Calibrated projection gives uniformly asymptotically valid confidence intervals for smooth functions in finite moment-restriction models.
A single marginal sensitivity parameter identifies probability of benefit without growing with covariate dimension.
Warning accuracy for a misclassified randomization test can be computed through adaptive integer programming.

body.tldr: Average efficacy can conceal simultaneous benefit and harm, while an imperfect binary endpoint assay makes even the two latent arm risks uncertain and couples them through one blinded channel. The proposal derives a unique probability-compatible latent-table root and proves that the sharp probability-of-benefit interval under a finite cross-product odds band is obtained from at most ten explicit channel candidates. It constructs attaining laws, separates closed-model endpoints from strict positive-cell attainment, and projects four exact binomial confidence sets through a finite contact-robust map with excess width of order \(1/(\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}})\).

project_justification.gap: Binary probability-of-benefit sensitivity analyses take the latent arm margins as observed, while direct misclassification methods do not exploit the special coupling created by one uncertain assay channel or the finite odds-band root geometry. Existing bound-inference work does not give finite-sample validation-binomial coverage through ties and assay-feasibility contacts.
project_justification.niche: A shared channel converts two separate margin intervals into a two-dimensional convex polygon whose nonlinear odds-root objective has an unusually small and explicitly classifiable stationary set.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the complete ten-candidate envelope, constructive sharpness, an exact strict-attainment criterion, and exact primitive confidence projection with a Youden-index width modulus.

body.related_work: ZhangNieSoonLiu2013, Section 3.3, supplies the fixed-margin binary odds reconstruction adapted in the compatible-root lemma. CiocaneaTeodorescuGabrielSjolander2025, Theorem 1 and its discussion of compatibility, provides the closest clean-outcome probability-of-benefit sensitivity formulation and the motivation arc from cancellation of benefit and harm. Molinari2008, equations (2.1)--(2.3), supplies the direct channel-matrix view and constructive interpretation of sharp latent distributions. GabrielSachsJensen2024 derives symbolic ordinal benefit bounds, evaluates bootstrap coverage, documents regular-bootstrap undercoverage near parameter-space boundaries, and reports a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) correction. The inference novelty here is limited to exact simultaneous inversion of the trial-risk and validation binomials coupled with the finite contact-complete shared-assay evaluator. FanPark2010 develops inference for switching sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds. KaidoMolinariStoye2019 supplies the calibrated-projection comparison, although the present procedure uses exact binomial inversion rather than asymptotic calibration. RossColeEdwardsEtAl2024 makes assay transport an explicit data-fusion condition rather than an implication of blinding. HengShaw2025 treats finite-population randomization tests under misclassification and motivates certified edge handling, but its target is warning accuracy rather than a superpopulation benefit interval. PolackEtAl2020 supplies the prospective clinical workflow: a blinded vaccine trial with a laboratory-confirmed binary endpoint, not evidence that a transported common assay channel already holds.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A floating-point generic optimizer missed a legal informativeness-edge minimum, returning \(0.1443566356\) instead of the explicit candidate value \(0.1320580555\). This is an implementation diagnostic, not a theorem contribution. Exact feasibility predicates and outward-rounded root evaluation remain necessary before empirical deployment.
body.honest_scope: The ten-point closed-model envelope, constructive endpoint attainment, strict-model bound transfer and exact strict-attainment criterion, exact projection, and \(O(1/(\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}}))\) width rate are proved above. The exact minimal universal evaluation cap remains open: ten is a proved complete candidate-map upper bound (eight when the informativeness cut is absent), not a proved minimum. Assay transport is maintained prospectively and is not inferred from trial blinding. Infinite odds endpoints, zero informativeness, covariate-dependent channels, and an empirical reanalysis of PolackEtAl2020 remain outside the formal claim.
